guide.title: SMS segments and what you actually pay for
guide.subtitle: Why the same text is sometimes one billable message and sometimes three
guide.excerpt: SMS is billed per segment, not per message. Whether your text fits in one segment depends on the character set it needs — and on the encoding you set on the connection.

p: The GSM-7 alphabet covers the letters, digits and punctuation needed for most Western European languages. Anything outside it — Chinese, Cyrillic, Arabic, emoji, curly quotes — forces the message into UCS-2, which has far less room per segment.

head: Encoding
Single segment
Per segment in a long message

p2: The per-segment figure is lower than the single figure because a long message is split across several parts, and each part carries a small header so the handset can reassemble them in order. That header is charged as part of the segment.

sections.h: A trailing detail that surprises people
p: A handful of characters — the euro sign, curly braces, backslash, tilde, caret — live in the GSM-7 extended table. They are representable in GSM-7, but each one occupies two septets instead of one, because it is sent as an escape sequence. A single one of them can be the character that pushes a 160-character message into a second segment.

sections.h: What the platform does with this
p: Segments are computed before the message is handed to the provider, and the count is kept on the record. That is the number your provider will bill you for, so you can reconcile the two without guessing.

Each connection carries an encoding setting. On the default, the platform inspects the text and picks GSM-7 if every character fits, otherwise UCS-2 — which is what the major providers do on their own side. You can also pin it: forcing GSM-7 makes a message containing a non-GSM-7 character fail outright rather than silently being transmitted as question marks or silently billed at double the segments.
sections.scope: Segment accounting applies to the SMS channel. It is a property of how SMS is transmitted and billed, and has no equivalent on the email or WhatsApp channels.

list: Keep marketing copy inside GSM-7 where you can — one stray curly quote can double a long message.
If a message must go out in a non-Latin script, budget roughly 70 characters per segment at the single-segment rate.
Check the segment count on the record before you compare it against a provider invoice; that is where a mismatch will show up first.
